scope: Joining weekly Viva Insights Person Query exports with Consumption, GitHub and Agent query exports into one person-week panel

input_requirements.recommendation: Use all four queries for a broader view of ways of working and AI usage across the products and activities they measure.
input_requirements.applicability: Apply file requirements, joins and source-specific checks only to the selected queries. Record omitted queries as unavailable, without inferring non-use.

naming_conventions.ids: File and dataset IDs are references within this guide's contract. They are not exported columns, file paths or required names for objects in your script.
naming_conventions.derived_datasets: Dataset labels describe intermediate summaries and the final panel that your script creates. Choose your own object names.
naming_conventions.week_start: WeekStart is this guide's chosen name for an aligned week-start date. It is not an extra column supplied by the exports. You may keep MetricDate or choose another name, provided every source uses the same week definition.

target_grain.rule: Export all selected queries grouped by week, with the same week start, wherever possible. This contract requires a weekly Person Query. `WeekStart` is its `MetricDate`. Consumption and GitHub default to daily, so change their grouping at setup. Use daily exports only when daily detail or week-start alignment is needed (G03, G03b).

coverage_assumption.scope: The configured population, date window and product filters of each supplied Viva Insights query.
coverage_assumption.missing_activity_rows: Inactive person-days are excluded by default. Within the query's scope, treat omitted activity rows as zero activity, including a person-week with no activity rows. This does not require separate completeness evidence.
coverage_assumption.exceptions: Keep unavailable queries, out-of-scope people or periods, null cells in existing rows and known export problems distinct from inactivity. Partial boundary weeks do not establish full-week totals.
coverage_assumption.eligibility: Activity zeros do not establish product eligibility or licence status. Use product-specific evidence for adoption denominators.

header_matching: Headers are listed in their raw export form, with spaces. The vivainsights R and Python packages replace spaces with underscores when they import a query, so `Collaboration hours` becomes Collaboration_hours. Treat the two forms as the same column. This applies to headers only, never to identifier values.
query_setup_recommendation: For all four queries, we recommend the Create analysis route because it offers more customisation parameters than dashboard exports.

queries.name: Person query
queries.access_context: The Person query is available only through this route. It gives you access to the full Person query metric list, including behavioural metrics such as Email hours, Meeting hours and Internal network size. Select the metrics you need when setting up the query.
queries.cadence: Weekly. Daily or monthly groupings are outside this contract.

missingness_states.meaning: A row exists with a positive value
A row exists with a recorded zero
No activity row within a supplied query's configured population and date window. Assume complete Viva Insights data and record zero activity
The query is unavailable, the person or period is outside its scope, a known export problem applies, or an absent non-activity measure has no defined zero interpretation. Keep as unknown
A row exists but the measure is null. Do not apply the omitted-inactive-row default to this cell
Not eligible for that product in the week
Not selected by the analysis cohort rule

gates.rule: Require the Person Query plus at least one of Consumption, GitHub or Agent. Record which queries are supplied and identify each export's layout. Within each selected query, files with `required_for_layout_match` set to true must all be present. If files or key columns differ from this contract, stop and record the difference.
Read identifiers as text. Do not change their case, trim them silently or fuzzy-match people.

Confirm weekly grouping from the Person Query configuration or equivalent export metadata, then validate one row per `PersonId` and `MetricDate` and detect the weekday of `MetricDate`. Stop if grouping is unknown, daily or monthly. Do not assume Monday or Sunday.

Record each fact export's configured date grouping from query setup or equivalent export metadata, then validate `MetricDate` against it. Sparse dates alone cannot establish cadence. Recommend weekly grouping for all queries. Daily and weekly exports are supported. A weekly export must start on the same weekday as the Person Query. Stop for unknown grouping, any other period such as monthly, or a different weekly start.
Assert uniqueness of each file's native key. Report duplicate counts and stop. Never keep an arbitrary first row.

Before summing Microsoft 365 credits across `SpendingPolicyId`, count person-service-period keys with more than one positive-credit row. If any exist, obtain a documented confirmation that the rows record disjoint consumption.
Sum `Session count` across `SpendingPolicyId` rows only when the documented confirmation explicitly covers sessions. Otherwise keep sessions per policy.
Join metadata many-to-one on unique keys. Report unmatched key counts without identifiers. Check that each `PeopleHistoricalId` maps to one `PersonId`.

Bring only panel-bound summaries to one row per `PersonId` and `WeekStart` before joining. Apply the measure rules: sum days only for configured daily exports, credits across policies only after G05, and sessions across policies only after G05b. Otherwise retain sessions per policy outside the panel. Keep GitHub breakdown dimensions as linked detail under G11. Never expand weekly rows into invented daily rows.
Left join each person-week summary onto the Person Query. Assert one-to-one, preserve the Person Query row count, and reconcile additive totals before and after.

Assume supplied Viva Insights queries are complete within their configured population, date window and product filters. Omitted activity rows represent inactivity by default, so record zero activity within that scope without requiring separate completeness evidence. Do not zero-fill unavailable queries, out-of-scope periods or people, null cells in existing rows, rolling indicators, limits, or known export problems. Record partial boundary weeks separately. Eligibility is a separate attribute: Microsoft 365 licence evidence never confirms GitHub eligibility.
Keep Microsoft 365 and GitHub credits in separate columns. Never derive tokens or currency from credits.
Do not join GitHub breakdown files wide. Keep them as linked detail tables.
Treat integration and cohort selection as separate, declared steps. An unavailable query does not establish non-use.
Record each variable's measurement window. Network sizes can repeat within a month and are averaged rather than summed.
Coverage, licence and additivity confirmations apply only to the export they were given for.

Check `PersonId` overlap between sources before joining. Investigate low overlap against activity filters, omitted inactive people and configured populations before concluding that pseudonymisation differs. Do not repair identifiers by matching on attributes.

Publish a group only when it contains at least 10 distinct people, counted with count_distinct(`PersonId`), in every filter and time slice. Withhold an entire related breakdown if remaining cells or totals would reveal a suppressed cell by subtraction. Never output identifiers.
Describe joined results as associations. Credits, sessions and actions do not measure value, quality or productivity.
